glosses: to put away, to lay aside

forms.form:
te zullen wegleggen
weg te zullen leggen

glosses: terzijde leggen
opbergen, achter slot brengen
To put (something) in its usual storage place; to place out of the way, clean up.

examples.text: Please put away the tools when you are finished.
I put the clothes away so as to neaten the room.

They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.

glosses: To store, add to one's stores for later use.

examples.text: putting a little away for a rainy day
Preparing for the worst, they put away food for the winter.

glosses: To consume (food or drink), especially in large quantities.

examples.text: You wouldn't think such a small person could put away so much food.
The blonde one, old Bernice, was drinking bourbon and water. She was really putting it away, too.

glosses: To send (someone) to prison or mental asylum.

examples.text: After he was convicted, they put him away for 10 years.

glosses: To kill someone.

examples.text:
It's Decoration Day.
And I knew the Hill Boys would put us away,
but my Daddy wasn't afraid.
He said "We'll fight till the last Lawson's last living day"

glosses: To knock out an opponent.

examples.text: He put away his opponent in the first round.

glosses: To discard, divest oneself of.

examples.text: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

glosses: To fend off, deflect; to dismiss.

examples.text: Also he told kynge Arthur that he shold mysse hym / yet had ye leuer than al your landes to haue me ageyne / A sayd the kynge / syn ye knowe of your aduenture puruey for hit / and put awey by your craftes that mysauenture / Nay said Merlyn it wylle not be / soo he departed from the kynge.

glosses: To divorce.

examples.text: And the pharyses cam and axed hym a question: whether it were laufull for a man to putt awaye hys wyfe.

glosses: To take a large lead in a game, especially enough to guarantee victory or make the game no longer competitive.

examples.text: They put the game away by scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter.

glosses: To strike out a batter.
To catch a fly ball or tag out a baserunner.
(pickleball) To hit the ball in such a way that the opponent cannot reach it; see passing shot
A place where items may be accumulated or routinely kept.

examples.text: This building used to be a store for old tires.

And his subjects wrung all they could wring
Out of temple and palace and store.

glosses: A supply held in storage.

examples.text: But there was an infinite store of mercy in those eyes, for him too a word of pardon even though he had erred and sinned and wandered.
By late summer a sufficient store of stone had accumulated, and then the building began[…], under the superintendence of the pigs.
What surprised us all was how Will's lighthearted nature and constant store of good humor won over one of the great heiresses of King Henry's court, Anne Bourchier.

glosses: A place where items may be purchased; a shop.

examples.text: I need to get some milk from the grocery store.

There was some laughter, and Roddle was left free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up […].”
In 1866 Colonel J. F. Meline noted that the rebozo had almost disappeared in Santa Fe and that hoop skirts, on sale in the stores, were being widely used.

glosses: Memory.

examples.text: The main store of 1000 36-bit words seemed large at the time.

glosses: A great quantity or number; abundance.

examples.text: I make my love engrafted to this store.

With store of Ladies, whose bright eies
Rain influence, and judge the prise
Of Wit, or Arms, while both contend
To win her Grace, whom all commend.

glosses: A head of store cattle (feeder cattle to be sold to others for finishing); a store cattle beast.
To keep (something) while not in use, generally in a place meant for that purpose.

examples.text: I'll store these books in the attic.

The half-dozen pieces […] were painted white and carved with festoons of flowers, birds and cupids. To display them the walls had been tinted a vivid blue which had now faded, but the carpet, which had evidently been stored and recently relaid, retained its original turquoise.
Following allocation to Toton on January 1 1996, it stayed there until transferral to Crewe in November 2000, before being stored at Eastleigh on December 17 the same year.

glosses: To contain.

examples.text: The cabinets store all the food the mice would like.

glosses: Have the capacity and capability to contain.

examples.text: They sell boxes that store 24 mason jars.

glosses: To write (something) into memory or registers.

examples.text: This operation stores the result on the stack.

glosses: To stock, to fill (a container, repository, etc.) with things.

examples.text: I have eaten my fill, and had my pockets well stored.
